summary: A reusable RAG object should carry claims, publisher identity, signature, verification methods, usage policy, privacy boundary, freshness, and revocation metadata.
An individual can publish a portable profile with public facts, private preferences, allowed use cases, consent boundaries, credentials, portfolio links, and revocable context bundles.
An organization can publish policies, service descriptions, support procedures, compliance statements, pricing references, API schemas, and approved pipeline primitives.
A government or regulator can publish verified laws, forms, eligibility rules, public notices, and machine-readable interpretations with effective dates and revocation handles.
Trust levels should separate authenticity from correctness: unsigned, self-signed, domain-verified, registry-verified, delegated authority, community-reviewed, and evaluated.
Every signed knowledge object should support stale-object handling through expiration, refresh cadence, signed tombstone, registry update, or key rotation record.
Retrieval pipelines must enforce whether an object may be retrieved, quoted, summarized, embedded, cached, transformed, exported, or used for model training.
